# Kharijite rebellion (682-693)

The Najdat rebellion, a Kharijite uprising, emerged during the Second Fitna as a factional opposition to Umayyad rule. Led by Najda ibn Amir al-Hanafi, the group established control over the region of Al-Yamama.
The Rebellion
By the Late 680s the Kharijite sub-group had expanded into Yemen and Hadhramaut, consolidating power over much of Arabia, and threatening the Hijaz, through raids and control of routes.
Their Defeat
Internal Fragmentations had split and weakend the group, as it would lead to the killing of Najda passing the groups leadership to Abu Fudayk, who continued resistance until their defeat by the Umayyads.
Aftermath
The defeat had removed the groups political ability, and the group declined and subsequently, lost all its members.
